Summary: BE-1: Bootstrap NestJS project and DB schema
Description:
As a developer, I want a NestJS project bootstrapped with PostgreSQL so that I can implement trip features consistently.

Acceptance Criteria:
- NestJS project initialized with modules: Auth, Trips, Checklist, Packing
- Connected to PostgreSQL with TypeORM/Prisma migrations
- Base entities created: User, Trip, TripTask, PackingItem
- Health-check endpoint available at /health

Summary: BE-2: Implement user authentication (email/password + JWT)
Description:
As a traveler, I want to sign up and log in so that my trips are saved securely to my account.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Endpoints: POST /auth/register, POST /auth/login, POST /auth/logout
- JWT-based auth; all trip endpoints require valid token
- Password is hashed (bcrypt)
- Return 401 for invalid credentials

Summary: BE-3: Trip CRUD API
Description:
As a developer, I want CRUD endpoints for trips so that the frontend can manage trip data.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Endpoints: POST /trips, GET /trips, GET /trips/:id, PATCH /trips/:id, DELETE /trips/:id
- Ownership check: user can only access their own trips
- Validation: end_date must be after start_date

Summary: DEV-1: CI pipeline and staging environment
Description:
As a developer, I want a CI pipeline and staging environment so that builds and deployments are reliable.

Acceptance Criteria:
- GitHub Actions/GitLab CI runs build + tests on every PR
- App deployed to GCP Cloud Run (or equivalent staging env)
- Cloud SQL connected to staging app
- Deployment triggered automatically on merge to main

Summary: TRIP-1: Create and view trips UI
Description:
As a traveler, I want to create a new trip and see all my trips listed so that I can stay organized.

Acceptance Criteria:
- 'My Trips' screen lists trips grouped into Upcoming and Past
- Each list item shows: destination, date range, status (Planning/In-progress/Completed)
- Trip creation form: name, destination, dates, trip type (leisure/business/road trip)
- Validation prevents invalid date ranges
- User can edit and delete a trip

Summary: TRIP-2: Trip dashboard overview
Description:
As a traveler, I want a dashboard for each trip so that I can see my planning progress at a glance.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Dashboard shows: trip name, destination, dates
- Shows pre-trip task progress (e.g. 5/12 done)
- Shows next upcoming pending task with due date
- Quick-links to Checklist, Packing, Itinerary, and Documents sections

Summary: CHK-1: Auto-generate default checklist on trip creation
Description:
As a traveler, I want the app to auto-generate a pre-trip checklist so that I don't forget common tasks like flights and insurance.

Acceptance Criteria:
- On trip creation, default tasks are inserted: Book flights, Book accommodation, Buy travel insurance, Check visa requirements, Arrange local transport, Buy eSIM/SIM, Exchange currency, Prepare travel documents
- Tasks are grouped into categories: Logistics, Documents, Money, Communication, Packing
- Tasks have suggested due dates relative to trip start (e.g. flights at T-60, insurance at T-30, packing at T-1)

Summary: CHK-2: Checklist CRUD API and UI
Description:
As a traveler, I want to manage my checklist items so that I can customize my trip planning.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Backend: list tasks by trip, add custom task, update status, delete task
- Frontend: checklist screen grouped by status (Pending/Done), sorted by due date
- User can add custom task (title, category, optional due date, notes)
- Completed tasks show a check mark and are visually greyed out
- User can uncheck a completed task

Summary: CHK-3: Overdue highlighting and filter controls
Description:
As a traveler, I want to filter and see overdue tasks so that I know what needs urgent attention.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Tasks where due_date < today and status != done are marked as overdue
- Overdue tasks highlighted in red or with a warning icon
- Filter controls: All / Pending / Completed / Overdue
- Overdue count shown on trip dashboard badge

Summary: PACK-1: Auto-suggest packing list on trip creation
Description:
As a traveler, I want the app to suggest a packing list based on my trip so that I pack efficiently.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Backend generates suggested items based on: trip duration, climate (warm/cold), and trip type
- Items grouped into: Clothes, Toiletries, Electronics, Documents, Misc
- User can accept all suggestions or selectively remove items
- Accessible via 'Packing' section of trip dashboard

Summary: PACK-2: Packing list CRUD UI with packed/unpacked toggle
Description:
As a traveler, I want to manage my packing list so that I can track what I've already packed.

Acceptance Criteria:
- User can add custom packing items and choose a category
- User can mark items as packed/unpacked with a checkbox
- List can be filtered by category or packed status
- Packing progress bar shown (e.g. 8/20 packed)

Summary: ITIN-1: DB schema and API for ItineraryDay and ItineraryItem
Description:
As a developer, I want itinerary entities and endpoints so that the frontend can build the day-by-day planner.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Entities: ItineraryDay (trip_id, date), ItineraryItem (day_id, type, title, notes, start_time, end_time, order_index, status)
- Endpoints: GET /trips/:id/itinerary, GET /itinerary-days/:id/items, POST/PATCH/DELETE for items
- Items auto-ordered by start_time

Summary: ITIN-2: Day-by-day itinerary builder UI
Description:
As a traveler, I want to build a day-by-day itinerary so that I have a clear plan for each day.

Acceptance Criteria:
- For each date in the trip range, show a 'Day X / Date' screen
- User can add/edit/delete items with: title, type (sightseeing/meal/transfer/other), start time, end time, notes
- Items are auto-ordered by start time
- Navigation between days via swipe or date picker

Summary: ITIN-3: Place entity and linking to itinerary items
Description:
As a traveler, I want to save and reuse places with addresses and coordinates so that my itinerary is location-aware.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Place entity: name, address, optional URL, optional lat/lng
- When creating/editing an itinerary item, user can choose existing place or create a new one inline
- Place details (address, link) shown on itinerary item
- Basic map pin shown if lat/lng is available

Summary: ITIN-4: Today view with current and next activity
Description:
As a traveler, I want a Today view that shows my current and next activities so that I can stay on track during the trip.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Today tab only visible when trip is active (today between start and end date)
- Shows current activity (based on time) and next upcoming activity
- User can mark items as Done or Skipped; these are excluded from 'Next activity' calculation
- If no activities remain, show 'You're done for today!'
- Shows linked documents shortcut on current activity card

Summary: ITIN-5: Adjust schedule when running late
Description:
As a traveler, I want to bulk-shift future activities by a set offset so that my plan stays realistic when I'm running late.

Acceptance Criteria:
- From Today view, user can tap 'Running late' and choose offset: +15, +30, +60 minutes
- All future (not yet started) items shift their start/end times accordingly
- Past and done items are unchanged
- Confirmation prompt shown before applying the change

Summary: NOTIF-1: Set up background job/queue service for reminders
Description:
As a developer, I want a background job queue so that notifications are reliable and run independently of API requests.

Acceptance Criteria:
- BullMQ + Redis (or equivalent) set up and connected
- Reminder entity: related_to_type, related_to_id, trigger_time, status (scheduled/fired/cancelled)
- API to schedule and cancel reminder jobs
- Jobs survive server restarts (persistent queue)

Summary: NOTIF-2: Pre-trip task reminders
Description:
As a traveler, I want reminders for upcoming and overdue pre-trip tasks so that I don't miss critical planning steps.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Reminder scheduled at due_date morning (default 09:00, user's timezone) for each TripTask
- Reminder fires again if task is overdue and still not done
- Push/local notification tapping opens the relevant task directly
- Trip-level toggle to enable/disable pre-trip reminders

Summary: NOTIF-3: Activity start reminders
Description:
As a traveler, I want reminders before each itinerary activity starts so that I know when to head to the next spot.

Acceptance Criteria:
- For each itinerary item with a start_time, schedule notification at start_time − lead_minutes
- Default lead time: 30 minutes (configurable in settings)
- Tapping notification opens Today view focused on that item
- Reminders are cancelled if the item is deleted or marked done early

Summary: DOC-1: Attach documents to a trip
Description:
As a traveler, I want to upload and store my booking confirmations and tickets in the app so that I can find them quickly when needed.

Acceptance Criteria:
- User can upload files (PDF, image) to a trip with a label (e.g. 'Flight to Tokyo', 'Hotel booking')
- Documents listed under trip with name, type, and upload date
- Tapping a file opens it in an in-app viewer
- User can delete a document

Summary: UX-1: Settings screen for timezone and reminder lead time
Description:
As a traveler, I want to configure my timezone and default reminder lead time so that notifications fire at the right time.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Settings screen with: timezone picker (auto-detected, editable) and default lead time for activity reminders (15/30/60 min)
- Backend uses user timezone for all reminder scheduling
- Do Not Disturb window setting (e.g. 23:00–07:00) suppresses notifications in that window

Summary: QA-1: End-to-end smoke tests for key flows
Description:
As a developer, I want end-to-end smoke tests for critical flows so that regressions are caught before release.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Test: Sign up → create trip → see auto-generated checklist and packing list
- Test: Create itinerary for one day, mark an item as done in Today view
- Test: Pre-trip reminder fires for a task due today
- Test: Activity reminder fires at start_time − lead_time
- Tests run in CI on every PR
